page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The CPU architecture includes hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES instructions, with an L3 cache capacity of 35 MB. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, necessitating network-attached disks for persistent storage needs, and comes with a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture optimized for parallel computing rather than single-threaded speed. The single-core metrics fall into the lower tiers, with a stress-ng score of 1107.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 995.0, alongside weak compression performance in gzip and single-threaded bzip3. However, multi-core throughput lands firmly in the middle tier, yielding 23637.07 on stress-ng, 8902.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and a PassMark CPU score of 23223.67. Uncached memory bandwidth measures 96.24 GB/sec for read operations and 48.07 GB/sec for writes, sustaining 22.63 million Redis SET operations per second.

The hardware tradeoffs for the ecs.g5.8xlarge reflect its older Skylake-generation architecture. While multi-threaded parallel throughput and static web serving capacity (17.15 GB/sec) remain solid, applications constrained by per-core execution speeds will encounter bottlenecks. Because storage relies entirely on remote volumes and no public IPv4 addresses are bundled by default, deployment planning requires account for external I/O configurations. The instance suits distributed web serving, container orchestration nodes, multi-threaded build environments, and in-memory caches where 128 GB of RAM and 32 vCPUs can be leveraged evenly.

Configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 128.0 GB of memory, it maintains a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing network block storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark evaluations reveal weaker single-thread metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 995.0, paired with average multi-threaded execution reaching a PassMark CPU score of 23223.67 and 22.63 million Redis SET operations per second. With instruction support for AVX-512, this instance fits concurrent enterprise workloads, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and scalable web serving that benefit from broad multi-core allocation.
